title: How Something Is Made or Done
writingModel: How a WKU Student ID Card Is Made

The WKU student ID card is a small document that carries a lot of information: the student's name, photograph, student number, faculty, and year of enrolment. But how is it produced? The process involves several careful steps.

First, the student's personal information is collected during registration. A form is completed by the student online, and a photograph is uploaded to the university system. The data is verified by the registration office to make sure all details are correct.

Once the data has been approved, it is sent to the printing department. A template is loaded, and the card is designed digitally — the name, photograph, and barcode are all placed in their correct positions. A proof version is generated and checked by a supervisor.

The physical card is then printed on a special plastic material. The surface is laminated to protect the printed information from damage. After lamination, the card is cut to the standard size and a small hole is punched in the corner so it can be attached to a lanyard.

The finished card is inspected for printing errors, incorrect information, or physical damage. Cards that pass inspection are packaged individually and sent to the relevant faculty office. Cards that fail the inspection are reprinted.

Finally, the card is collected by the student from their faculty office or delivered directly to their dormitory. The whole process, from registration to delivery, typically takes between five and ten working days.

A student ID card may seem like a simple object. But the process by which it is created, checked, approved, printed, inspected, and delivered involves many people, many stages, and a great deal of careful attention.
